criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale. Include the following required information: What is the spacecraft's primary mission? Why is the mission needed? How many spacecraft are used and why? Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Primary mission (reef/ocean monitoring with fluid lensing), rationale (bleaching, acidification, GBR value) and single-spacecraft justification explained. Users/operators identified (CSIRO, BOM, university/government). References included, though some are non-academic URLs.

evidence.quote: coral reef and ocean monitoring. The satellite must provide images for a fluid lensing tool
Only one satellite is required. This also just allows for simplicity in communications
would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM)

criteria.name: Main body: mission design. Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate. Include relevant screenshots and software files in the main body of the report and/or appendix. Include the following information: Where will it launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? Which ground control facilities will you use? How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Launch site, vehicle, orbit type (SSO retrograde polar), characteristics, Keplerian elements, maneuver (direct injection, EOL drag sail), ground station and access statistics with STK screenshots provided. Some technical inaccuracies (RAAN as launch site, Vega E not yet flown) and reliance on Wikipedia timeline limit depth.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear engineering structure with executive summary, contents, sections, figures labelled, access table. Grammar readable; OCR artefacts not penalised. References listed but citation style inconsistent and URLs used, including Wikipedia.

evidence.quote: This report outlines the intended designs and procedures involved in the construction of a Earth observation satellite
STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart

technical_issues.issue: Claims RAAN initial value indicates launch facility location; RAAN defined by inertial frame, not launch latitude. Inclination-altitude relation plot correct but argument of latitude used instead of true anomaly without full Keplerian set.

Selected Vega E whose first launch planned 2024 and relies on future 2025 SSMS mission; justification based on Wikipedia 'Timeline of spaceflight' not primary source; piggyback orbit matching assumed.

No delta-v or drag-sail sizing calculation; uncontrolled deorbit from 600km with drag sail needs analysis of deorbit time <25yr rule; small-sat without propulsion claimed but drag sail deployment still requires system.

overall: Solid preliminary SSO mission for GBR reef monitoring with STK evidence supporting launch, 600km/97.79deg orbit, ground contacts and 5-year lifespan with drag-sail EOL. Well structured and meets most requirements, limited by weak launch sourcing and missing propulsion analysis.

feedback.summary: You produced a solid SSO mission for GBR reef monitoring with clear STK evidence. You justified a single spacecraft, CSIRO/BOM users, Guiana launch on Vega E, 600km/97.79deg SSO, Mount Pleasant contacts and 5-year EOL with drag sail. Well-structured work, limited by launch source credibility and missing propulsion/deorbit analysis.
next_steps: Replace Wikipedia timeline with ESA/Arianespace primary sources and validate Vega E availability; assess Vega C backup with orbit-matching constraints.
Correct orbital mechanics: show full Keplerian set with true anomaly, and clarify RAAN is inertial, not launch latitude. Size drag sail and show deorbit <25yr with delta-v/drag budget.
Upgrade referencing format and strengthen literature support for fluid-lensing requirements and SSO lighting rationale.

criteria.C1: You clearly defined primary mission for coral reef fluid-lensing monitoring, rationale on bleaching and GBR value, and justified single satellite simplicity. Users CSIRO/BOM identified well. To reach top of Accomplished, add detailed payload requirements and peer-reviewed references instead of URLs.
criteria.C2: You provided launch (Vega E, Guiana), 600km/97.7924° SSO, a=6971km, ground station Mount Pleasant with access stats and STK Figures like Image 4. For higher Accomplished, fix RAAN interpretation, justify launch vehicle with primary sources, and add calculations for manoeuvres and drag-sail EOL.
criteria.C3: Your conclusion summarises launch, polar SSO for illumination, ground station trade and Vega C contingency linked to bleaching need. To strengthen, synthesize quantitative results from orbit access and duration analysis and state explicit outcomes rather than general statements.
criteria.C4: Clear engineering structure with Executive Summary, contents, labelled STK 3D views and access tables, readable writing. To reach top of Accomplished, use consistent citation style throughout, replace Wikipedia/NOAA URLs with academic sources, and ensure reference list matches in-text citations.
